source.title: Interpreting ResNet-based CLIP via Neuron-Attention Decomposition

record.tranche_reason: The study measures the dimensionality of decomposed representations in CLIP-ResNet, a vision model setting, rather than in toy superposition models or LLMs.
record.gate_note: The rank-one reconstruction results bear on V6 and are recorded below. The paper's sparse-contribution, polysemanticity, sub-concept, segmentation, and distribution-shift results do not test feature competition under dimensional limits or the other claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. Its rank-one result is about each CLIP-ResNet neuron-head path's output contribution, across images, lying along one direction in the image-text embedding space. That measures how many dimensions a computation path's output spans, not whether superposed features are 1-D directions (V6). There are no feature dictionaries, no capacity pressure and no superposition measure. Polysemanticity is observed via inertia, but nothing tests its cause (V2/V3). The only link to the claim is a citation of Lecomte et al. on polysemanticity.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also note that neuron-head pairs remain polysemantic, though less so than neurons, and that some pairs represent sub-concepts of their neuron's concept.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes pretrained CLIP-ResNet computation paths and their reconstruction properties; it does not use toy feature-learning networks or test a sparsity-dependent superposition transition.

fits_no_version.finding: In CLIP-RN50x16/x64, neuron-head path contributions reconstructed from one principal component keep ImageNet accuracy (70.7%, 73.9%). Neuron contributions need several components (66.9% to 70.0%, and 71.0% to 73.3%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual computation-path (neuron-head) output contributions in CLIP-ResNet are approximately rank-one; neuron-level contributions are multi-dimensional.

fits_no_version.finding: Neuron-head pairs remain polysemantic but are less so than neurons, by top-10-image inertia (Fig. 3); some pairs encode sub-concepts of their neuron.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finer path-level decomposition reduces, but does not eliminate, polysemanticity in vision models.

record.peer_reviewed: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025) Workshop: Mechanistic Interpretability
record.problems: The dimensionality evidence is indirect: it is inferred from downstream classification accuracy after principal-component reconstruction, and the study does not measure superposition or feature overlap under a capacity constraint.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. Other reported measurements, including mean-ablation sparsity, text-description reconstruction, segmentation scores, and distribution-shift correlations, do not test the versions recorded here.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweeps or geometry.
All: no test of capacity as the cause of polysemanticity.
All: polysemanticity is observed but its origin is not tested.
All: no LLMs, no measure of features spread across neurons, no SAE.
Dimensionality of superposed features: only the rank of path output contributions is measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the PCA-reconstruction rows to V6 on the strength of the word "one-dimensional". The construct is the rank of a component's output across images, not the dimensionality of superposed features, so I moved the rows to fits_no_version and gave no verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity, overlap under dimensional limits, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity, or whether importance determines which features get dedicated dimensions.
The study reports polysemantic components but does not test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure or whether it is evidence of superposition.
LLM representations, features spread across neurons, and sparse features recovered by an SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The study measures dimensionality of neuron and neuron-head contributions, but does not test actual superposition or identify the dimensions of features under capacity pressure.

rows.subject: OpenAI's CLIP-RN50x16
rows.operation_detail: Reconstructed image representations using the first principal component of each neuron-head contribution and measured ImageNet classification accuracy.
rows.note: The paper says this reconstruction causes no decrease in classification accuracy, consistent with neuron-head contributions being approximated by a single direction.
rows.check: Measures the rank of a neuron-head path's output contribution, not the dimensionality of superposed features; does not bear on V6.

rows.subject: OpenAI's CLIP-RN50x16
rows.operation_detail: Reconstructed image representations using the first principal component of each neuron contribution and measured ImageNet classification accuracy.
rows.note: The paper describes this as an approximately 4% accuracy drop, in contrast to the neuron-head result.
rows.check: A neuron's summed contribution across heads spanning more than one direction is not evidence about multi-dimensional superposed features; does not bear on V6.

rows.subject: OpenAI's CLIP-RN50x16
rows.operation_detail: Reconstructed image representations using the first two principal components of each neuron contribution and measured ImageNet classification accuracy.
rows.note: The two-component reconstruction improves on the one-component neuron result but remains below baseline.

rows.subject: OpenAI's CLIP-RN50x16
rows.operation_detail: Reconstructed image representations using the first three principal components of each neuron contribution and measured ImageNet classification accuracy.
rows.note: The three-component reconstruction improves on the one-component neuron result but remains below baseline.

rows.subject: OpenAI's CLIP-RN50x16
rows.operation_detail: Reconstructed image representations using the first four principal components of each neuron contribution and measured ImageNet classification accuracy.
rows.note: Four components approach but do not reach the stated baseline.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: One-component neuron-head contributions in CLIP-RN50x16 and CLIP-RN50x64
reader_labels.reason: One principal component preserves the reported ImageNet accuracy for both models (r1, r6), consistent with these decomposed contributions being approximately one-dimensional.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Neuron-only contributions in CLIP-RN50x16 and CLIP-RN50x64
reader_labels.reason: One principal component falls below baseline, and additional components improve reconstruction (r2-r5, r7-r9); the rank-one finding is specific to neuron-head contributions, not neuron contributions generally.
